how_to_apply: Applications are accepted only in online mode; applications received through any other mode will be rejected. To apply for HP High Court Apply Online:
Visit the official recruitment portal at hphcrecruitment.in, or the relevant link on the High Court website at highcourt.hp.gov.in.
Go through the FAQs and video tutorial available on the recruitment portal before starting the application.
Register and fill in the Online Recruitment Application (ORA) form with personal, educational, and category details.
Upload the required photograph, signature, and certificates in the specified size and format.
Pay the applicable examination fee through online mode only.
Preview the completed application and download a printout or screenshot for your records before final submission.
Once submitted, the application cannot be withdrawn or modified. It can only be cancelled without a refund of the fee.
important_instructions: Candidates must ensure their eligibility regarding qualification, category, age, and experience as on the last date of submission of the online application. Candidates will be informed about examination/test schedules only through SMS alerts and registered email; no separate call letters will be sent through any other mode. Category once claimed will be treated as final, and no change will be entertained. The number of vacancies may increase or decrease, and vacancies in a particular division or district may vary due to administrative reasons. Re-checking or re-evaluation of answer sheets is not allowed at any stage. Results against regular vacancies will be declared first, followed by results for contractual and daily wages modes. Candidates cannot switch between appointment modes after final results are declared. Candidates should apply only once for a particular post and need not apply separately for its regular, contractual, and daily wages vacancies.

content_sections.heading: HP High Court Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Educational qualification requirements differ by post for HP High Court Recruitment 2026: Court Manager: Graduation in any stream with a Master's in Business Administration (MBA) from a UGC-recognized University or Institution in India, plus 3 years' experience in Process Management, IT Systems Management, Human Resources Management, or Financial Management. Good knowledge of legal affairs and computer applications is desirable. Clerk: Graduation from a recognized University with basic computer knowledge, including operating Windows and Linux, and typing/printing. Stenographer Grade-III: Graduation degree from a recognized University. Driver: Matriculation pass from a recognized Board, a valid LMV driving licence held for at least 3 years, and at least 3 years' experience driving an LMV. Preference is given to candidates with good mechanical knowledge of automobiles. Process Server: 10+2 pass from a recognized Board. Peon/ Orderly/ Chowkidar/ Safai Karamchari/ Chowkidar-cum-Safai Karamchari: 10+2 pass from a recognized Board. Candidates must also be citizens of India and, except Bonafide Himachalis, must have passed matriculation, 10+2, or graduation (Group-C posts) or middle, matriculation, or 10+2 (Group-D posts) from a school or institution situated within Himachal Pradesh, along with knowledge of the customs and dialects of the State. Age is reckoned as on 1 January 2026: A 5-year relaxation in the upper age limit is admissible only to bonafide SC, ST, OBC candidates of HP and persons with benchmark disabilities of HP, where the post is reserved for these categories. Age relaxation for HP Government employees is admissible as per applicable orders and instructions. Before submitting the application, candidates are advised to verify that they meet the required age criteria. Use our Age Calculator to calculate your exact age as per the official cut-off date.

content_sections.heading: HP High Court Recruitment 2026 Selection Process
content_sections.text: The selection process differs by post: Court Manager: Written Test and Viva-voce, as per Schedule-III Part 3 (Phase-I and Phase-II) of the R&P Rules, 2022. Clerk: Screening Test, Written Test, Typing Test, and Document Verification (DV). Candidates must qualify a typing test with a speed of 30 WPM in English and 25 WPM in Hindi (Kruti Dev-10 font), held separately after qualifying the Screening Test. Stenographer Grade-III: Screening Test as per the syllabus on the official website, followed by a Stenography Test at 80 WPM in English with accurate transcription within 5 times the dictation time, and a Typing Test at 40 WPM in English and 30 WPM in Hindi (Kruti Dev-10 font). Candidates making more than 10% mistakes in transcription or typing are declared unqualified. Driver: Screening Test, Proficiency Test of driving, and Document Verification. Process Server: Screening Test, Written Test, and Evaluation, as per Part 10 of Schedule-III of the R&P Rules, 2022. Peon/Orderly/Chowkidar/Safai Karamchari/Chowkidar-cum-Safai Karamchari: Candidates are shortlisted in a 1:3 ratio for Evaluation/Document Verification based on marks in 10+2 (calculated out of 85 marks) plus 15 marks for evaluation of uploaded documents. The final merit list is based on the combined score.

content_sections.heading: HP High Court Recruitment 2026 Required Documents
content_sections.text: Candidates must keep the following scanned documents ready before filling the online application: Recent coloured photograph on a white background (20 to 50 KB, JPG/JPEG/PNG) Signature on a white background (10 to 20 KB, JPG/JPEG/PNG) Matriculation certificate as age proof (100 to 500 KB, JPG/JPEG/PNG) ID proof such as Aadhaar, driving licence, or passport (100 to 500 KB, JPG/JPEG/PNG) Other certificates and documents, including category and educational certificates (100 KB to 2 MB, PDF only)

faq.question: Q1. What is HP High Court Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is a recruitment drive by the High Court of Himachal Pradesh for 388 posts of Court Manager, Clerk, Stenographer Grade-III, Driver, Process Server, and Peon/Orderly/Chowkidar/Safai Karamchari on the Establishment of District Judiciary in Himachal Pradesh.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in HP High Court Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: A total of 388 vacancies are available across six post categories, covering regular, contractual, and daily wages appointments.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for HP High Court Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The online application closes on 10 September 2026 at 11:59 PM.

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification required for HP High Court Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It varies by post, ranging from 10+2 pass for Process Server and Peon-category posts to graduation for Clerk and Stenographer, and graduation with MBA for Court Manager.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for HP High Court Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: For Court Manager, it is 25 to 35 years. For other posts, UR/EWS candidates must be 18 to 45 years, while reserved HP categories and HP Government employees can apply up to 50 years, as on 1 January 2026.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee for HP High Court Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Rs. 450 (including GST) for Unreserved candidates and Rs. 300 (including GST) for reserved categories of HP (SC, ST, OBC, EWS, PH), payable only online.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply online for HP High Court Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Applications must be submitted online through hphcrecruitment.in before the last date; applications submitted through any other mode will not be accepted.

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process for HP High Court Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It differs by post and includes combinations of Screening Test, Written Test, Typing Test, Stenography Test, Driving Proficiency Test, Viva-voce, and Document Verification, as specified for each post.

faq.question: Q9. What is the salary for HP High Court Recruitment 2026 posts?
faq.answer: Regular posts carry Pay Matrix levels ranging from Rs. 18,000–56,900 (Process Server, Peon-category posts) to Rs. 48,700–1,54,300 (Court Manager). Contract and daily wages posts carry wages fixed by the Government of Himachal Pradesh.
